title: A minimal component attains the dimension maximum
statement: Let k be a field and S a commutative finite type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let p be a prime ideal and d,r natural numbers with dim(S_p)=d [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and trdeg_k(kappa(p))=r [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. There exists a minimal prime q of S contained in p with dim(S/q)=d+r.

proof.text: Apply the dimension/transcendence-degree theorem to the domain S/p. Its fraction field is canonically kappa(p) by the Mathlib IsFractionRing instance, so hr identifies dim(S/p) with r. Prime quotient correspondence identifies this dimension with the coheight of p in PrimeSpectrum S.

For any prime q contained in p, let P be the corresponding prime of S/q. The comap map is strictly monotone and its image is the primes containing q, an upper set, so it preserves coheight and height(P) is at most height(p). The domain common-maximal-chain-length theorem implies dim(S/q) = height(P) + coheight(P): choose longest chains below and above P, prove extremality of the endpoints and saturation of consecutive pairs by contradiction using cons, snoc and insertNth, join the chains with smash, use the existing private saturated_isMaxChain_of_nonempty theorem via a proof-only import all of Sheaf.RingTheory.FiniteTypeDomainDimensionLocalRingChains to show maximality, and apply the common-length theorem to their maximal range. This is proved locally in the private pure_dimension_sum helper.

The localization dimension/height correspondence and hd give height(p)=d. Mathlib exists_series_of_height_eq_coe supplies a length-d chain ending at p. Its head q is minimal: a smaller prime would prepend to a length-(d+1) chain below p, contradicting height(p)=d. Lift the whole chain through the quotient prime order isomorphism to S/q; its length gives d<=height(P), and strict monotonicity of comap gives the reverse inequality. Thus height(P)=d, and the preceding domain identity yields dim(S/q)=d+r.
